title: The first-person incident report
description: A pilot or controller describing something that nearly went wrong, filed voluntarily and stripped of identifying detail. The most emotionally restrained prose in English about genuinely frightening events.
features: First person and past tense; emotion is absent and consequences are stated flatly
Decisions are elected, implying deliberation under procedure
Heavy abbreviation and role capitalisation with no glossary
Certainty about own actions; hedging about causes and other people
Closes with a return to normality
specimen: At approximately 40 minutes into the flight, the crew observed an unexpected indication on the secondary panel. I elected to transfer control and run the associated checklist. It could not be determined whether the indication was spurious. The flight continued without further incident and no injuries were reported.

title: The compliance warning
description: A regulator telling a named company it has broken the law, in a form designed to establish legal notice. Direct second person, absolute authority, zero aggression.
features: Addresses you while the agency names itself in third person
Every accusation is anchored to a dated inspection and numbered regulation
A deadline and consequence appear near the end
Closing disclaimer says the list is not exhaustive
Severity is carried by citations, not adjectives
specimen: During an inspection of your facility conducted on 3–7 March 2026, our investigator documented deviations from the applicable requirements. You failed to maintain records adequate to demonstrate compliance. Within fifteen working days of receipt of this letter, notify this office in writing of the steps taken. This letter is not intended to be an all-inclusive list of deviations.
phrasebook: may result in legal action without further notice

title: The pleading
description: Complaints, motions and briefs filed in federal court. Numbered-paragraph prose in which every fact is attributed, qualified, or pleaded.
features: Numbered paragraphs with one assertion each
Upon information and belief marks claims not personally verified
Terms are defined once and reused exactly
Parties are named by role
Requests come last in a WHEREFORE clause
specimen: 14. Upon information and belief, Defendant maintained the equipment at the facility described in Paragraph 9 (the "Facility"). 15. At all times relevant hereto, Defendant was aware of the condition. 16. Plaintiff realleges and incorporates by reference the foregoing paragraphs.

title: The clinical narrative
description: A physician describing one patient's course for other physicians. The person is compressed into age, sex and presenting complaint.
features: Formulaic opener: age, sex, duration, complaint
Passive voice removes the clinician as subject
Findings precede interpretation
Negatives are stated explicitly
Systematic understatement
Consent sentence near the end
specimen: A 54-year-old man presented with a three-day history of intermittent symptoms. Initial examination was unremarkable. Laboratory studies were notable for two abnormal values. He was started on supportive therapy. Findings were consistent with, though not diagnostic of, the suspected process.
phrasebook: presented with a X-day history of
the patient was discharged in stable condition

title: The normative specification
description: Internet standards prose with formally graded modal verbs and a strict division between requirements and explanation.
features: MUST, SHOULD, MAY and MUST NOT have defined force
Normative and informative text are structurally separate
Scope is fenced early
Security Considerations is mandatory
Terminology is defined before use
specimen: For the purposes of this document, the term refers only to the case described in Section 3. Implementations MUST reject malformed input. It is RECOMMENDED that deployments log such events. Behaviour under partial failure is out of scope for this specification.
phrasebook: for the purposes of this document

title: The oversight finding
description: An auditor telling a government agency it is doing something badly, with total politeness and precision.
features: Finding, reason for study, and recommendations open the report
Recommendations name an official and verifiable action
Quantities are bounded at the edges
Scope and methodology disclose limits
Agency response is printed with the auditor's reply
specimen: In at least 12 of the 40 cases reviewed, required documentation was not retained. As of March 2026, the agency had not established a tracking mechanism. We recommend that the Administrator develop and implement written procedures. The agency concurred with our recommendation.
phrasebook: in at least N of the M cases reviewed
we conducted this performance audit in accordance with
we provided a draft of this report for review and comment

title: The rule and its preamble
description: A government explaining a new rule and answering every objection raised by the public.
features: Rigid agency/action/summary/dates header
Comment is restated fairly before response
Narrow concession can accompany broad refusal
Agency writes as we and calls it this final rule
Effective and compliance dates stay distinct
specimen: Comment: Several commenters stated that the proposed threshold was impractical. Response: We agree in part. After further consideration, we have revised the threshold as described in Section III.B. This final rule is effective 60 days after publication.

title: The risk factor
description: A company legally obliged to describe everything that could go wrong while promising nothing; built from conditionals and qualifiers.
features: Conditional catastrophe is the dominant sentence shape
Could and may dominate; will is rare
Forward-looking disclaimer fences predictions
Risks are ordered roughly by materiality
Management Discussion is warmer than Risk Factors
specimen: We may be unable to retain key personnel. If we are unsuccessful in doing so, our operations could be materially and adversely affected. We cannot assure you that our mitigation efforts will be effective. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties.
phrasebook: could be materially and adversely affected
in the ordinary course of business
to the extent we are unable to

title: The log line
description: Text a program wrote about itself, at speed, with no reader in mind. The most rigid register in the corpus.
features: Fixed timestamp, host, process/pid, level, message order
No articles and no subjects
Severity is a token
Repeated events are byte-identical except variable fields
Identifiers, durations and truncation dominate
Nothing is explained or softened
specimen: 2026-08-25T04:12:07.481Z host-07 sshd[24188]: WARN auth: connection refused from 10.4.2.19 after 3 attempts (2.104s)

title: The stack trace
description: A runtime describing its own death: structurally rigid, language-specific, and sensitive to frame order and indentation.
features: Frame order differs by language
Indentation and punctuation are mechanical
Paths include realistic dependency noise
Exception line is type plus terse lowercase message
Chained exceptions use fixed connecting sentences
specimen:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/app/handlers/queue.py", line 214, in dispatch
    result = self._resolve(payload)
KeyError: 'target_id'
phrasebook: During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred
The above exception was the direct cause of

title: The blameless postmortem
description: An engineering organisation explaining its own outage in public under a formal convention against naming the responsible person.
features: Actors are systems, scripts, or changes rather than people
Fixed summary, impact, timeline, root cause, factors, actions order
Impact is quantified before explanation
Timeline entries approach log register
Action items are verifiable and owned
We means the company
specimen: Impact. For approximately 47 minutes, 3.1% of requests returned errors. No customer data was affected. Root cause. A configuration change was deployed without passing validation. Action items. We are adding a pre-deploy check, tracked in ISSUE-4471.
phrasebook: this incident was not the result of a security issue

title: The vulnerability advisory
description: Disclosure of a flaw, written to be machine-parsed and legally careful. Impact is conditional: what an attacker could do, never what anyone did.
features: Fixed identifier, severity, score, affected/patched versions metadata
Impact names attacker position and conditional ability
Version boundaries are exact
Workarounds and fixes are separate
Reporter credit closes the document
Score carries severity without drama
specimen: An attacker with authenticated access to the management interface could cause the service to terminate unexpectedly. Versions 2.1.0 through 2.4.0 are affected; the issue is fixed in 2.4.1. Users unable to upgrade should restrict interface access at the network layer. Reported by an external researcher.
phrasebook: no known exploitation in the wild

title: The man page
description: Dense, impersonal reference documentation with a section structure that has barely changed since the 1970s.
features: Fixed NAME, SYNOPSIS, DESCRIPTION, OPTIONS, EXIT STATUS, SEE ALSO order
NAME is command, dash, lowercase phrase
Present tense third person states behaviour as fact
Edge cases are bare conditionals
Cross-references include section numbers
Undefined and unspecified are technical terms
specimen:
NAME
    fsync - synchronise a file's in-core state with storage
DESCRIPTION
    If the descriptor does not refer to a file, the behaviour is unspecified.
    On success, zero is returned. On error, -1 is returned and errno is set.

title: The API reference
description: Documentation for a function, written for someone who already knows the language; only what it does, not motivation or persuasion.
features: The function is grammatical subject: Returns, Raises, Accepts
Parameters follow signature order with types and defaults
Version markers use fixed vocabulary
Failure modes sit beside success
Notes and warnings are callouts
The reader is almost never addressed
specimen: Returns a list of matching records. If limit is omitted, defaults to 100. Raises ValueError if the cursor has been closed. Deprecated since version 4.2: use iter_records() instead.

title: The bug report
description: A defect described for reproduction: a rigid structured report followed by a looser conversational thread.
features: Steps, expected, actual, environment skeleton
Reproduction steps are numbered one-action imperatives
Environment is key-value pairs
Status vocabulary is small and fixed
Thread shifts into first-person conversational register
Regressions are bounded by version
specimen:
Steps to reproduce: 1. Open the settings panel. 2. Toggle sync off. 3. Restart the client.
Expected: sync remains disabled. Actual: sync re-enables on launch.
Reproducible on build 4471, not on 4468.

title: The review comment
description: One engineer criticising another's work in front of the team using a grammar of softened criticism.
features: Prefixes carry severity: nit, optional, blocking
Criticism is phrased as a question
Imperatives are hedged
Scope defence proposes a follow-up
Approval is abbreviated and unemotional
Warmth is load-bearing
specimen: nit: naming here is inconsistent with the module above. Is the early return intentional? Might be worth pulling this into a helper. Not blocking — happy to take it as a follow-up.
phrasebook: can we pull this out into
please add a test for this
out of scope for this PR
let's handle that as a follow-up

title: The commit message
description: A short change description written in imperative mood, with every convention visible at once.
features: Imperative subject: Fix, never Fixed or Fixes
Short subject, blank line, then why rather than what
Trailers use key-colon-value
Type prefixes form a closed vocabulary
Changelogs use categories and past tense
No hedging
specimen:
fix(auth): reject tokens with a missing audience claim

Tokens issued before 4.1 omitted the claim entirely, so the check silently passed. No functional change for current issuers.

Fixes: #4471
phrasebook: fix / feat / chore / refactor / docs / test

title: The README and its neighbours
description: The front door of a repository. It shifts from warm description to terse imperative usage to flat reference inside one file.
features: Register changes by section
Install and usage use second-person imperatives
Code blocks carry information; prose stays short
One-line description says what and for what
Warnings are callouts
Constraints are ranges in a predictable place
Lower sections converge on API reference
specimen:
# queuectl
A small CLI for inspecting and draining job queues.

## Installation
Requires Python 3.10 or later.
    pip install queuectl

## Usage
Run the following to list pending jobs:
    queuectl list --pending

> Note: draining is not reversible.
